article.headline: Making Films Like Books: Magnific Bets on Solo AI Cinema
article.lede: When Joaquín Cuenca Abela writes that “we will make films like we write books,” he is not offering outside commentary — he is the CEO of Magnific, the Spanish AI creative platform that just integrated Seedance 2.0, ByteDance’s latest video-generation model, into its Business and Enterprise tiers. The launch spans more than 150 countries. The United States is not among them, for reasons that a copyright dispute with Hollywood studios makes fairly plain.
article.body:
Seedance 2.0, developed by ByteDance’s research division Seed, is unusual among *generative video* models in its treatment of audio. Most competitors produce video first and attach sound in post-processing; Seedance 2.0 generates audio and video in a single **joint pass**, so a character speaking in a large reverberant room will have acoustically appropriate sound without manual adjustment. The model accepts up to nine reference images, three video clips, and three audio clips simultaneously, produces 15-second multi-shot sequences with consistent characters, and offers multilingual lip-sync in more than eight languages. Its *@reference system* — which enforces visual style and character identity across shots via uploaded reference material — is the feature most cited by early reviewers as a primary differentiator; OpenAI, for context, announced it would wind down its rival Sora video model later in 2026.

The US exclusion is not incidental. Within 24 hours of ByteDance unveiling Seedance 2.0 in February 2026, Walt Disney (DIS) and three other major studios sent cease-and-desist letters alleging copyright infringement; the Motion Picture Association followed with what it characterised as its first C&D directed at a generative AI company. ByteDance subsequently suspended the global rollout. Neither ByteDance nor Magnific has issued a formal statement linking the US delay to the legal pressure — the launch announcement says only “rolling out soon” — but the timeline leaves little interpretive room. American creators may access Seedance 2.0 through ByteDance’s own CapCut platform on a separate track.

The platform offering Seedance 2.0 has its own condensed history. Freepik was founded in 2010 in Málaga as a library of images and vector graphics — effectively a search engine for free visual assets — and spent a decade growing under majority ownership by private equity firm EQT (EQT.ST). When generative AI arrived in force, Cuenca pivoted the company toward creative tools. In May 2024, Freepik acquired Magnific, a Murcia-based startup whose AI image-upscaling tool had accumulated 725,000 users without paid marketing; in April 2026, the parent company retired the Freepik brand and unified the stack under the acquired product’s name. The company now reports $230 million in *ARR* — annualised recurring revenue — with over one million paying subscribers. It is private; EQT holds a majority stake.

Cuenca’s central thesis — that solo creators will produce films as routinely as they write books — depends on AI eliminating the cost and logistics of production crews, locations, and equipment. Seedance 2.0 is a credible step: its reference-based consistency and native audio synthesis make single-creator video pipelines more tractable than earlier tools allowed. But the analogy has limits. Writing a book requires a keyboard and time; a film is judged against a visual tradition built by thousands of practitioners over a century. Whether “making a film” and “making something that looks like a film” remain distinct categories is the question this technology raises but cannot yet answer.

concepts.definition: AI systems that synthesise video content from text, image, or audio prompts — producing novel footage rather than retrieving or editing pre-existing clips. Outputs are typically short (under 30 seconds) and generated on demand from a description or reference input.

An architecture in which a model produces audio and video simultaneously in a single computational pass, rather than generating video first and adding sound afterward. Because both modalities are produced together, sound design — reverb, acoustics, ambient noise — is inherently coherent with the visual scene.

Seedance 2.0’s mechanism for maintaining visual and audio consistency across generated shots. Users upload reference images, clips, or audio to anchor the model’s output, so the same character appearance, visual style, or voice persists throughout a multi-shot sequence.

A metric used by subscription businesses to express recurring revenue as a yearly figure, typically calculated by multiplying current monthly subscription revenue by twelve. It is a forward-looking run-rate estimate, not a measure of revenue actually earned over a trailing twelve months.

The alignment of a generated character’s mouth movements with accompanying speech audio. In AI video models, ‘multilingual lip-sync’ means the model can synthesise realistic facial articulation for speech across multiple languages, not just the primary language of the training data.

A formal legal letter demanding that the recipient immediately stop a specified activity — here, allegedly generating video that reproduces or derives from copyrighted film content. A C&D is not itself a lawsuit but signals a credible litigation threat and commonly precedes one.

article.fact_check: The tweet describes Freepik as “the world’s biggest AI creative suite.” This is not straightforwardly verifiable: Canva, with a larger registered user base, and Adobe Creative Cloud, with deeper enterprise penetration, both contest the claim depending on the metric used. By raw monthly web traffic, Freepik/Magnific is genuinely among the largest creative platforms — third-party data from Semrush puts it at approximately 173 million visits in March 2026. The “over 100 million monthly visits” figure cited in the announcement is technically accurate but meaningfully understated relative to current data.

ticker_dis.name: The Walt Disney Company
ticker_dis.blurb: Disney is a global media and entertainment conglomerate whose assets span theme parks, film studios (Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm), the ABC broadcast network, ESPN, and the Disney+ and Hulu streaming platforms. The company has undergone significant restructuring under returning CEO Bob Iger, who returned in 2022 to stabilise the company after a turbulent period under his successor. Disney's streaming transition has been costly but Disney+ reached profitability in late 2024.
ticker_dis.recent: Disney reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $93 billion. The experiences segment (theme parks and cruises) remains the primary profit engine. The company is pursuing ESPN's transition to a direct-to-consumer streaming service and has made moves to consolidate streaming assets. Paul Pelosi sold 10,000 shares of DIS per the January 2026 PTR disclosure.

ticker_eqt-st.name: EQT AB
ticker_eqt-st.blurb: EQT AB is a Swedish private equity firm founded in 1994, focused on investments in mid-market companies across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific. It manages multiple funds spanning venture, growth, buyout, and infrastructure strategies. EQT is one of the largest private equity firms in Europe by assets under management.

poster_cuenca.blurb: Joaquín Cuenca Abela is a Spanish entrepreneur and engineer, co-founder of Panoramio (acquired by Google) and currently CEO of Freepik. He posts about technology, startups, AI, and photography. His follower count is not publicly available.
